findings.claim: narrowing validate_required/2 from @castable_fields to @required_fields does not weaken any security-relevant guarantee
findings.evidence: Read lib/letflow/service_catalog/version.ex directly. request_schema/response_schema/retry_policy are the only fields dropped from the required list; all three are still passed through Ecto.Changeset.cast/3 against @castable_fields so they remain properly typed (no raw/unvalidated pass-through) -- validate_required/2 only controls presence, not type safety. Confirmed against priv/repo/migrations/20260921000003_add_service_catalog_versioning.exs that these three columns (request_schema, response_schema, retry_policy on service_catalog_versions) are genuinely nullable in the DB (no null: false), so the Ecto-level requiredness now matches the schema's actual constraint instead of over-constraining it. Also traced archive_changeset/1's only caller: lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex archive_current_version/1 (line ~360-379) builds attrs entirely from an already-fetched %Entry{} struct's own fields, not from raw external/user-controlled input, so there is no injection or validation-bypass surface introduced by these fields being optional in the changeset.

findings.claim: removing chk_service_catalog_version_length CHECK constraint does not reopen a length-based DoS/overflow concern -- varchar(255) column type genuinely enforces the same bound
findings.evidence: The removed constraint (check: char_length(version) <= 255) applied to service_catalog.version, added at migration line 37 as `add :version, :string, null: false, default: "1"` with no `size:` override -- Ecto's :string type defaults to Postgres varchar(255), which enforces the identical 255-char bound at the column-type level (an INSERT/UPDATE exceeding it is rejected by Postgres itself, independent of the now-removed CHECK). down/0 was updated consistently (its own `drop constraint` for the removed one was also removed, and no dangling reference remains).
